__inputs.name: DS_BIGQUERY
__inputs.label: BigQuery datasource
__inputs.description: The Grafana BigQuery data source to query.

title: BQAA Public Demo
description: Public-sharing build of bqaa-dashboard.json. Everything a public dashboard cannot evaluate has been removed: templating.list is empty, panel SQL carries no dashboard-variable interpolation, hourly buckets come from BigQuery's own TIMESTAMP_TRUNC instead of Grafana's frontend time-group macros, the cost rates are hardcoded literals, no panel reads another panel's result through the "-- Dashboard --" datasource (that resolution happens in the browser and never runs for an anonymous viewer, so such panels render empty), and the per-session Trace detail panel is gone so no raw event timeline is exposed. Every stat therefore issues its own BigQuery query — set a BigQuery Custom Quota on the project before sharing, as grafana/README.md describes. The 72-hour window is enforced in the SQL itself — every panel filters on timestamp >= TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 72 HOUR) rather than Grafana's time-range macro. A hidden time picker only removes the widget; a from/to pair in the URL still reaches the backend, so a macro-based range would let any viewer widen the BigQuery scan at will. Keep the bound in SQL: it holds no matter how the dashboard is shared or what the URL says. timepicker.refresh_intervals is empty and refresh is off so a viewer cannot pin the dashboard to a fast auto-refresh, editable is false, and timezone is utc to match the UTC buckets TIMESTAMP_TRUNC produces. Before importing, replace the literal YOUR_PROJECT_ID and YOUR_DATASET_ID placeholders in every panel's SQL (see the sed shortcut in grafana/README.md) and confirm adk_ matches your ViewManager view prefix. Do not point this at real production telemetry; seed a dedicated demo dataset instead. Edit bqaa-dashboard.json, not this file, for interactive use.

panels.title: Sessions
panels.description: Distinct session_ids in the locked 72-hour range.

targets.rawSql:
-- Panel: Sessions stat (Overview row).
-- Distinct session_ids in the locked 72-hour range.
-- Public-demo build: no dashboard variables, so no Agent / User / Session /
-- Event Type filter clauses appear below and the stat covers the whole range.
-- Each Overview stat carries its own query rather than reading this one back
-- through the "-- Dashboard --" datasource. That datasource is resolved in the
-- browser against another panel's already-fetched result, and a public
-- dashboard rendered for an anonymous viewer never performs that resolution,
-- so every dependent panel came up empty. The price is one BigQuery scan per
-- stat instead of one for the whole row — see grafana/README.md on setting a
-- BigQuery Custom Quota to bound what that can cost.
-- Replace YOUR_PROJECT_ID and YOUR_DATASET_ID before importing.
-- The 72-hour bound is a hardcoded predicate, not Grafana's time-range macro.
-- Hiding the time picker is a frontend affordance only: a URL time range still
-- reaches the backend, so the macro would let a viewer widen the scan. Keeping
-- the bound in SQL is what caps it. Do not restore the macro here.
-- HAVING COUNT(*) > 0 keeps the no-data contract: an unaggregated SELECT over
-- aggregates always emits one row, so an empty range would otherwise report a
-- confident "0 sessions" instead of letting the stat panel fall back to its
-- "No matching data" text.
SELECT
  COUNT(DISTINCT session_id) AS sessions
FROM `YOUR_PROJECT_ID.YOUR_DATASET_ID.agent_events`
WHERE timestamp >= TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 72 HOUR)
HAVING COUNT(*) > 0

panels.title: Events
panels.description: Total agent_events rows in the locked 72-hour range.

targets.rawSql:
-- Panel: Events stat (Overview row).
-- Total agent_events rows in the locked 72-hour range.
-- Public-demo build: no dashboard variables, so no filter clauses.
-- This stat runs its own query rather than reading the Sessions panel's result
-- through the "-- Dashboard --" datasource, which a public dashboard rendered
-- for an anonymous viewer never resolves. See the Sessions panel SQL.
-- The 72-hour bound is a hardcoded predicate, not Grafana's time-range macro:
-- hiding the time picker does not stop a URL time range from reaching the
-- backend, so only the SQL caps the scan.
-- HAVING COUNT(*) > 0 keeps the no-data contract: an unaggregated SELECT over
-- an aggregate always emits one row, so an empty range would otherwise report a
-- confident "0 events" instead of letting the stat panel fall back to its
-- "No matching data" text.
SELECT
  COUNT(*) AS events
FROM `YOUR_PROJECT_ID.YOUR_DATASET_ID.agent_events`
WHERE timestamp >= TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 72 HOUR)
HAVING COUNT(*) > 0

panels.title: Error rate
panels.description: Share of events counted as errors: event_type ending in _ERROR, or a non-NULL error_message, or UPPER(status) = 'ERROR'. See grafana/queries/README.md.

targets.rawSql:
-- Panel: Error rate stat (Overview row).
-- Share of events in the locked 72-hour range counted as errors: event_type
-- ending in _ERROR, or a non-NULL error_message, or UPPER(status) = 'ERROR'.
-- The same predicate the Errors over time panel charts.
-- Public-demo build: no dashboard variables, so no filter clauses.
-- This stat runs its own query rather than reading the Sessions panel's result
-- through the "-- Dashboard --" datasource, which a public dashboard rendered
-- for an anonymous viewer never resolves. See the Sessions panel SQL.
-- The 72-hour bound is a hardcoded predicate, not Grafana's time-range macro:
-- hiding the time picker does not stop a URL time range from reaching the
-- backend, so only the SQL caps the scan.
-- SAFE_DIVIDE rather than / so a zero denominator yields NULL, not an error.
-- HAVING COUNT(*) > 0 keeps the no-data contract: an unaggregated SELECT over
-- aggregates always emits one row, so an empty range would otherwise report a
-- confident "0%" instead of letting the stat panel fall back to its
-- "No matching data" text.
SELECT
  SAFE_DIVIDE(
    COUNTIF(ENDS_WITH(event_type, '_ERROR') OR error_message IS NOT NULL OR UPPER(status) = 'ERROR'),
    COUNT(*)
  ) AS error_rate
FROM `YOUR_PROJECT_ID.YOUR_DATASET_ID.agent_events`
WHERE timestamp >= TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 72 HOUR)
HAVING COUNT(*) > 0

panels.title: Avg LLM latency
panels.description: Mean total_ms across LLM responses. Reads 'No matching data' rather than 0 when the range holds no LLM latency telemetry.

targets.rawSql:
-- Panel: Avg LLM latency stat (Overview row).
-- Mean total_ms over the typed llm_responses view, the scalar companion to the
-- LLM latency percentiles panel in the LLM & FinOps row.
-- Public-demo build: no dashboard variables, so no filter clauses.
-- This stat runs its own query rather than reading the Sessions panel's result
-- through the "-- Dashboard --" datasource, which a public dashboard rendered
-- for an anonymous viewer never resolves. See the Sessions panel SQL.
-- The 72-hour bound is a hardcoded predicate, not Grafana's time-range macro:
-- hiding the time picker does not stop a URL time range from reaching the
-- backend, so only the SQL caps the scan.
-- No IFNULL: AVG stays NULL when latency telemetry is missing, so the panel
-- reads "No matching data" instead of a fake 0 ms.
-- HAVING COUNT(*) > 0 keeps the no-data contract: an unaggregated SELECT over
-- an aggregate always emits one row, so an empty range would otherwise emit a
-- row at all instead of letting the stat panel fall back to its
-- "No matching data" text.
SELECT
  AVG(total_ms) AS avg_llm_latency_ms
FROM `YOUR_PROJECT_ID.YOUR_DATASET_ID.adk_llm_responses`
WHERE timestamp >= TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 72 HOUR)
HAVING COUNT(*) > 0

panels.title: Events over time
panels.description: Event volume per event_type, in fixed one-hour buckets.

targets.rawSql:
-- Panel: Events over time, one series per event_type (Overview row).
-- Public-demo build: no dashboard variables, so no filter clauses.
-- Buckets are fixed at one hour via BigQuery's native TIMESTAMP_TRUNC rather
-- than Grafana's time-group/interval macros. Public dashboards render for
-- anonymous viewers, where those frontend macros are not resolved and the query
-- fails to parse. Macro names are omitted from this comment on purpose: Grafana
-- expands macros textually, without honouring SQL comments.
-- The 72-hour bound is likewise a hardcoded predicate rather than the
-- time-range macro: hiding the time picker does not stop a URL time range from
-- reaching the backend, so only the SQL caps the scan.
SELECT
  TIMESTAMP_TRUNC(timestamp, HOUR) AS time,
  event_type,
  COUNT(*) AS events
FROM `YOUR_PROJECT_ID.YOUR_DATASET_ID.agent_events`
WHERE timestamp >= TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 72 HOUR)
GROUP BY time, event_type
ORDER BY time

panels.title: Errors over time
panels.description: Error events per event_type, in fixed one-hour buckets. An event counts as an error when event_type ends in _ERROR, error_message is non-NULL, or UPPER(status) = 'ERROR'. An empty panel reads "No errors in range": the query returns no rows, which is not a broken panel. It cannot tell "no errors" apart from "no events at all" — check the Overview stat panels, which read "No matching data" when the range holds nothing.

targets.rawSql:
-- Panel: Errors over time, one series per event_type (Overview row).
-- Public-demo build: no dashboard variables, so no filter clauses.
-- Buckets are fixed at one hour via BigQuery's native TIMESTAMP_TRUNC rather
-- than Grafana's time-group/interval macros, which are not resolved for
-- anonymous viewers of a public dashboard.
-- The 72-hour bound is likewise a hardcoded predicate rather than the
-- time-range macro: hiding the time picker does not stop a URL time range from
-- reaching the backend, so only the SQL caps the scan.
SELECT
  TIMESTAMP_TRUNC(timestamp, HOUR) AS time,
  event_type,
  COUNT(*) AS errors
FROM `YOUR_PROJECT_ID.YOUR_DATASET_ID.agent_events`
WHERE timestamp >= TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 72 HOUR)
  AND (ENDS_WITH(event_type, '_ERROR') OR error_message IS NOT NULL OR UPPER(status) = 'ERROR')
GROUP BY time, event_type
ORDER BY time

panels.title: Events by agent
panels.description: Event volume per agent over the raw agent_events table. Events written without an agent group under "unknown" rather than being dropped, so the bars add up to the Events stat above.

targets.rawSql:
-- Panel: Events by agent (Overview row).
-- Event volume per agent over the raw agent_events table, so every event type
-- counts, not just the ones a typed view exposes.
-- Public-demo build: no dashboard variables, so no filter clauses.
-- agent is nullable on the raw table; IFNULL groups those rows under "unknown"
-- rather than dropping them, so the bars still add up to the Events stat above.
-- The output column is agent_name, not agent, so the GROUP BY names the IFNULL
-- alias instead of resolving back to the raw nullable column.
-- HAVING COUNT(*) > 0 is a written-down contract rather than a live filter: the
-- GROUP BY already emits no rows when nothing matches, which is what lets the
-- panel fall back to its "No matching data" text. Stating it next to the
-- aggregate keeps a later edit that widens the input set (an outer join, or a
-- COUNTIF replacing the count) from silently drawing zero-height bars.
SELECT
  IFNULL(agent, 'unknown') AS agent_name,
  COUNT(*) AS events
FROM `YOUR_PROJECT_ID.YOUR_DATASET_ID.agent_events`
WHERE timestamp >= TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 72 HOUR)
GROUP BY agent_name
HAVING COUNT(*) > 0
ORDER BY events DESC

panels.title: Top error messages
panels.description: Distinct error_message strings in range, most frequent first, capped at 50. Only events carrying a non-NULL error_message appear: an error that recorded no message (event_type ending in _ERROR, or UPPER(status) = 'ERROR', with a NULL error_message) has no string to group under, so these counts are a subset of what Errors over time charts. sessions and agents count the distinct sessions and agents that hit each message; last_seen is the most recent occurrence in range. PRIVACY: error strings can carry prompt or user content — review this panel before sharing the dashboard.

targets.rawSql:
-- Panel: Top error messages (Overview row).
-- Ranks the distinct error_message strings in the window by how often they
-- occur, so the loudest failure mode is the first row.
-- Public-demo build: no dashboard variables, so no filter clauses.
-- Scope: only events carrying a non-NULL error_message. An error event that
-- recorded no message (event_type ending in _ERROR, or UPPER(status) = 'ERROR',
-- with error_message NULL) has no string to group under and is intentionally
-- absent, so these counts are a subset of what Errors over time charts.
-- HAVING COUNT(*) > 0 is a written-down contract rather than a live filter: the
-- GROUP BY already emits no rows when nothing matches, which is what lets the
-- panel fall back to its "No errors in range" text. Stating it next to the
-- aggregate keeps a later edit that widens the input set (an outer join, or the
-- error predicate moved out of the WHERE into a COUNTIF) from silently listing
-- zero-count rows.
SELECT
  error_message,
  COUNT(*) AS errors,
  COUNT(DISTINCT session_id) AS sessions,
  COUNT(DISTINCT agent) AS agents,
  MAX(timestamp) AS last_seen
FROM `YOUR_PROJECT_ID.YOUR_DATASET_ID.agent_events`
WHERE timestamp >= TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 72 HOUR)
  AND error_message IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY error_message
HAVING COUNT(*) > 0
ORDER BY errors DESC
LIMIT 50

panels.title: Token usage over time
panels.description: Prompt / completion / total tokens from adk_llm_responses, in fixed one-hour buckets. Missing usage telemetry degrades to 0.

targets.rawSql:
-- Panel: Token usage over time (LLM & FinOps row).
-- Uses the typed llm_responses view. Missing usage telemetry
-- degrades to 0 for sums (IFNULL) rather than dropping the bucket.
-- Public-demo build: no dashboard variables, so no filter clauses.
-- Buckets are fixed at one hour via BigQuery's native TIMESTAMP_TRUNC rather
-- than Grafana's time-group/interval macros, which are not resolved for
-- anonymous viewers of a public dashboard.
-- The 72-hour bound is likewise a hardcoded predicate rather than the
-- time-range macro: hiding the time picker does not stop a URL time range from
-- reaching the backend, so only the SQL caps the scan.
SELECT
  TIMESTAMP_TRUNC(timestamp, HOUR) AS time,
  IFNULL(SUM(usage_prompt_tokens), 0) AS prompt_tokens,
  IFNULL(SUM(usage_completion_tokens), 0) AS completion_tokens,
  IFNULL(SUM(usage_total_tokens), 0) AS total_tokens
FROM `YOUR_PROJECT_ID.YOUR_DATASET_ID.adk_llm_responses`
WHERE timestamp >= TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 72 HOUR)
GROUP BY time
ORDER BY time

panels.title: LLM latency (p50 / p95 / TTFT)
panels.description: Latency percentiles from adk_llm_responses, in fixed one-hour buckets. Gaps mean missing latency telemetry.

targets.rawSql:
-- Panel: LLM latency percentiles + time-to-first-token (LLM & FinOps row).
-- Latency aggregates deliberately stay NULL when telemetry is missing so
-- the chart shows gaps instead of fake zeros.
-- Public-demo build: no dashboard variables, so no filter clauses.
-- Buckets are fixed at one hour via BigQuery's native TIMESTAMP_TRUNC rather
-- than Grafana's time-group/interval macros, which are not resolved for
-- anonymous viewers of a public dashboard.
-- The 72-hour bound is likewise a hardcoded predicate rather than the
-- time-range macro: hiding the time picker does not stop a URL time range from
-- reaching the backend, so only the SQL caps the scan.
SELECT
  TIMESTAMP_TRUNC(timestamp, HOUR) AS time,
  APPROX_QUANTILES(total_ms, 100)[OFFSET(50)] AS p50_total_ms,
  APPROX_QUANTILES(total_ms, 100)[OFFSET(95)] AS p95_total_ms,
  APPROX_QUANTILES(ttft_ms, 100)[OFFSET(50)] AS p50_ttft_ms
FROM `YOUR_PROJECT_ID.YOUR_DATASET_ID.adk_llm_responses`
WHERE timestamp >= TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 72 HOUR)
GROUP BY time
ORDER BY time

panels.title: Tokens by model
panels.description: Token totals grouped by model_version (response-side attribute).

targets.rawSql:
-- Panel: Tokens by model (LLM & FinOps row).
-- model_version is the response-side attribute exposed by the
-- llm_responses view; rows without it group under "unknown".
-- Public-demo build: no dashboard variables, so no filter clauses.
SELECT
  IFNULL(model_version, 'unknown') AS model,
  IFNULL(SUM(usage_prompt_tokens), 0) AS prompt_tokens,
  IFNULL(SUM(usage_completion_tokens), 0) AS completion_tokens,
  IFNULL(SUM(usage_total_tokens), 0) AS total_tokens,
  COUNT(*) AS responses
FROM `YOUR_PROJECT_ID.YOUR_DATASET_ID.adk_llm_responses`
WHERE timestamp >= TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 72 HOUR)
GROUP BY model
ORDER BY total_tokens DESC

panels.title: Estimated cost (placeholder rates)
panels.description: DERIVED estimate, not telemetry: token counts x placeholder rates of $1.25 per 1,000,000 input tokens and $5.00 per 1,000,000 output tokens, hardcoded in the panel SQL because a public dashboard cannot read dashboard variables. Edit those two literals in the query to match the pricing of the model(s) you run. USD per 1,000,000 tokens is the unit model price lists publish, and the same unit bqaa-dashboard.json's price_per_1m_input_tokens / price_per_1m_output_tokens variables use, so a rate copies across between the two files unchanged. Token counts are the primary FinOps signal.

targets.rawSql:
-- Panel: "Estimated Cost" stat (LLM & FinOps row).
-- Costs are DERIVED, not telemetry: the SDK records token counts only.
-- Public-demo build: the rates are hardcoded literals below rather than
-- dashboard variables, because a public dashboard evaluates no variables.
-- Both are read as USD per 1,000,000 tokens — the unit model price lists
-- publish — hence the /1e6 divisors. Edit the two literals to match the
-- pricing of the model(s) you actually run. This is the same unit
-- bqaa-dashboard.json's price_per_1m_input_tokens / price_per_1m_output_tokens
-- variables use, and the same defaults, so a rate copies across unchanged.
-- The panel is intentionally labeled "Estimated Cost" for this reason;
-- token counts are the primary FinOps signal.
-- The Total tokens stat below runs its own query rather than reading this
-- one's result through the "-- Dashboard --" datasource, which a public
-- dashboard rendered for an anonymous viewer never resolves — so no
-- total_tokens column is selected here.
-- HAVING COUNT(*) > 0 keeps the no-data contract: an unaggregated SELECT over
-- aggregates always emits one row, so an empty range would otherwise report a
-- confident zero cost instead of letting the panel fall back to its
-- "No matching data" text.
SELECT
  IFNULL(SUM(usage_prompt_tokens), 0) / 1e6 * 1.25    -- $ / 1M input tokens
    + IFNULL(SUM(usage_completion_tokens), 0) / 1e6 * 5.00  -- $ / 1M output tokens
    AS estimated_cost_usd
FROM `YOUR_PROJECT_ID.YOUR_DATASET_ID.adk_llm_responses`
WHERE timestamp >= TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 72 HOUR)
HAVING COUNT(*) > 0

panels.title: Total tokens
panels.description: Sum of the provider-reported usage.total token count (usage_total_tokens in adk_llm_responses) over the locked 72-hour range. This is the provider's own total rather than prompt + completion added up here, so it can differ from that sum when a provider bills cached, reasoning or other tokens it does not report in those two fields.

targets.rawSql:
-- Panel: Total tokens stat (LLM & FinOps row).
-- The provider-reported usage.total count, not prompt + completion added up
-- here, so it can exceed that sum when a provider bills cached or reasoning
-- tokens it does not report in those two fields.
-- Public-demo build: no dashboard variables, so no filter clauses.
-- This stat runs its own query rather than reading the Estimated cost panel's
-- result through the "-- Dashboard --" datasource, which a public dashboard
-- rendered for an anonymous viewer never resolves. See the Sessions panel SQL.
-- The 72-hour bound is a hardcoded predicate, not Grafana's time-range macro:
-- hiding the time picker does not stop a URL time range from reaching the
-- backend, so only the SQL caps the scan.
-- HAVING COUNT(*) > 0 keeps the no-data contract: an unaggregated SELECT over
-- an aggregate always emits one row, so an empty range would otherwise report a
-- confident "0 tokens" instead of letting the stat panel fall back to its
-- "No matching data" text.
SELECT
  IFNULL(SUM(usage_total_tokens), 0) AS total_tokens
FROM `YOUR_PROJECT_ID.YOUR_DATASET_ID.adk_llm_responses`
WHERE timestamp >= TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 72 HOUR)
HAVING COUNT(*) > 0

panels.title: LLM calls
panels.description: Count of LLM_RESPONSE events in range — the number of completed model calls the rest of this row aggregates over. Read from adk_llm_responses, which holds exactly that one event type. Divide the token and cost panels by this to get a per-call average.

targets.rawSql:
-- Panel: LLM calls (LLM & FinOps row).
-- Total number of LLM_RESPONSE events in the window: the call volume the token,
-- latency and cost panels in this row are averaging and summing over. The
-- llm_responses view holds exactly one event type, so COUNT(*) is the
-- LLM_RESPONSE count by construction.
-- Public-demo build: no dashboard variables, so no filter clauses.
-- HAVING COUNT(*) > 0 keeps the no-data contract: an unaggregated SELECT over an
-- aggregate always emits one row, so an empty range would otherwise report a
-- confident "0 calls" instead of letting the stat panel fall back to its
-- "No matching data" text.
SELECT
  COUNT(*) AS llm_calls
FROM `YOUR_PROJECT_ID.YOUR_DATASET_ID.adk_llm_responses`
WHERE timestamp >= TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 72 HOUR)
HAVING COUNT(*) > 0

panels.title: Tool invocations by tool
panels.description: Invocations per tool from adk_tool_starts, so failed invocations are counted (adk_tool_completions would drop them).

targets.rawSql:
-- Panel: Tool invocations by tool (Tools row).
-- Uses the typed tool_starts view so failed invocations are included in the
-- volume (the tool_completions view would drop them).
-- Public-demo build: no dashboard variables, so no filter clauses.
SELECT
  tool_name,
  COUNT(*) AS invocations
FROM `YOUR_PROJECT_ID.YOUR_DATASET_ID.adk_tool_starts`
WHERE timestamp >= TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 72 HOUR)
GROUP BY tool_name
ORDER BY invocations DESC

panels.title: Tool latency
panels.description: Per-tool latency; NULLs mean missing latency telemetry.

targets.rawSql:
-- Panel: Tool latency by tool (Tools row).
-- Latency stays NULL when missing (no IFNULL) so averages aren't skewed.
-- Public-demo build: no dashboard variables, so no filter clauses.
SELECT
  tool_name,
  COUNT(*) AS completions,
  AVG(total_ms) AS avg_ms,
  APPROX_QUANTILES(total_ms, 100)[OFFSET(50)] AS p50_ms,
  APPROX_QUANTILES(total_ms, 100)[OFFSET(95)] AS p95_ms
FROM `YOUR_PROJECT_ID.YOUR_DATASET_ID.adk_tool_completions`
WHERE timestamp >= TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 72 HOUR)
GROUP BY tool_name
ORDER BY p95_ms DESC

panels.title: Tool errors
panels.description: TOOL_ERROR events plus completions that carry a non-NULL error_message or UPPER(status) = 'ERROR'. UNION ALL is intentional: one logical failure that emits both a TOOL_ERROR and an error-status TOOL_COMPLETED appears as two rows. PRIVACY: this table shows session IDs and raw error strings — review it before sharing the dashboard.

targets.rawSql:
-- Panel: Tool errors (Tools row).
-- Combines the dedicated TOOL_ERROR view with any error-status completions.
-- UNION ALL intentionally preserves both telemetry records when one logical
-- failure emits a TOOL_ERROR and an error-status TOOL_COMPLETED event.
-- Public-demo build: no dashboard variables, so no filter clauses.
SELECT
  timestamp,
  agent,
  session_id,
  tool_name,
  error_message
FROM `YOUR_PROJECT_ID.YOUR_DATASET_ID.adk_tool_errors`
WHERE timestamp >= TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 72 HOUR)

UNION ALL

SELECT
  timestamp,
  agent,
  session_id,
  tool_name,
  error_message
FROM `YOUR_PROJECT_ID.YOUR_DATASET_ID.adk_tool_completions`
WHERE timestamp >= TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 72 HOUR)
  AND (error_message IS NOT NULL OR UPPER(status) = 'ERROR')
ORDER BY timestamp DESC
LIMIT 100

panels.title: Recent sessions
panels.description: Session rollups over the raw agent_events table, capped at the 250 most recently active sessions in the locked 72-hour range. session_errors_in_window counts events whose event_type ends in _ERROR, or that carry a non-NULL error_message, or whose UPPER(status) = 'ERROR'. session_users_in_window lists every distinct user_id in the session, so it can name more than one. session_input_tokens_in_window / session_output_tokens_in_window sum $.usage.prompt / $.usage.completion over the session's LLM_RESPONSE events — the same values the LLM & FinOps panels report as prompt/completion tokens. There is no click-through: the interactive dashboard's Trace detail panel is deliberately absent from this public build. PRIVACY: session and user IDs are shown verbatim — review this panel before sharing the dashboard.

targets.rawSql:
-- Panel: Recent sessions (Sessions row).
-- Session-level rollup over the raw agent_events table.
-- Public-demo build: no dashboard variables, so no filter clauses and no
-- HAVING LOGICAL_OR(...) guards. Every rollup below covers every event the
-- session has in the window, so the columns tie out against the Overview stats.
-- session_id IS NOT NULL keeps events written without a session from
-- collapsing into one NULL row that names no session.
-- The LIMIT caps the table at the 250 most recently active sessions in the
-- window.
-- session_users_in_window is a STRING_AGG rather than ANY_VALUE: nothing in the
-- schema stops two user_ids from sharing a session, and ANY_VALUE would silently
-- name one of them. It reads like COUNT(DISTINCT agent) below — the column is
-- there to show when a session is not the single-user thing it was assumed to
-- be, so it lists every user rather than picking one.
-- The token columns read $.usage.prompt / $.usage.completion straight off the
-- raw content payload: this panel groups the raw table, so it cannot use the
-- typed adk_llm_responses view that exposes the same two extractions to the LLM
-- & FinOps panels as usage_prompt_tokens / usage_completion_tokens. Only
-- LLM_RESPONSE carries a usage block, and the IF() says so explicitly rather
-- than leaning on the path being absent from every other event type's content.
SELECT
  session_id,
  STRING_AGG(DISTINCT user_id, ', ' ORDER BY user_id) AS session_users_in_window,
  MIN(timestamp) AS started_in_window_at,
  MAX(timestamp) AS last_event_in_window_at,
  TIMESTAMP_DIFF(MAX(timestamp), MIN(timestamp), SECOND) AS duration_in_window_s,
  COUNT(DISTINCT agent) AS session_agents_in_window,
  COUNT(*) AS session_events_in_window,
  COUNTIF(ENDS_WITH(event_type, '_ERROR') OR error_message IS NOT NULL OR UPPER(status) = 'ERROR') AS session_errors_in_window,
  IFNULL(SUM(IF(event_type = 'LLM_RESPONSE',
    SAFE_CAST(JSON_VALUE(content, '$.usage.prompt') AS INT64), NULL)), 0)
    AS session_input_tokens_in_window,
  IFNULL(SUM(IF(event_type = 'LLM_RESPONSE',
    SAFE_CAST(JSON_VALUE(content, '$.usage.completion') AS INT64), NULL)), 0)
    AS session_output_tokens_in_window
FROM `YOUR_PROJECT_ID.YOUR_DATASET_ID.agent_events`
WHERE timestamp >= TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 72 HOUR)
  AND session_id IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY session_id
ORDER BY last_event_in_window_at DESC
LIMIT 250
